a.text:
'The Sky is blue and fine,
The Breeze lilts by in Song;
The River murmurs clear,
My Heart is filled with Hope.
The Mist parts overnight,
The Earth welcomes Dawn's Light;
Praise be Leithanien,
Where free Men find their Home.'
—Lied des klaren Himmels (1078)

steps.name: Hibiscus
steps.text: (According to the map, I shouldn't be far from the Rhodes Island branch office now.)

steps.name: Hibiscus
steps.text: (Got held up a bit coming into Vyseheim, but if I just hurry up, I can hopefully make it there before I'm late...)

steps.name: Passionate Infected
steps.text: Hold it right there!

steps.name: Hibiscus
steps.text: Er... me?

steps.name: Passionate Infected
steps.text: Yes indeed, you, beautiful Dame! You're an unfamiliar face. Could this be your first time here in the Afterglow?

steps.name: Hibiscus
steps.text: Yes, I'm a Rhodes Island Operator, here to look into the Serendipitous Infected Prognosis Phenomenon—

steps.name: Passionate Infected
steps.text: Leave behind your work and duties for now. I cordially invite you here to perform with me in song!

steps.name: Hibiscus
steps.text: Perform?

steps.name: Hibiscus
steps.text: But I bought this concert flute as a staff. I couldn't play you a single song...

steps.name: Passionate Infected
steps.text: No matter! If you can just make it sing, I have faith I can spin your notes into a song to offer to you, Dame. Let's commemorate this fine day!

steps.name: Hibiscus
steps.text: I have an appointment with someone, and I'm almost late as is.

steps.name: Passionate Infected
steps.text: Don't worry, don't worry. Anyone would let a little delay go, with weather so fine.

steps.name: Passionate Infected
steps.text: Come, this won't take long!

steps.name: Hibiscus
steps.text: I... I just play some random notes then?

steps.name: Passionate Infected
steps.text: Please!

steps.name: Hibiscus
steps.text: (Alright, alright, I can make it sound...)

steps.name: Passionate Infected
steps.text: Do... fa... la.. so... fa... mi...

steps.name: Passionate Infected
steps.text: Wonderful, a motif full with hope!

steps.name: Passionate Infected
steps.text: Emma, I'll play. What if you and our visitor dance a tune together?

steps.name: Hibiscus
steps.text: Together?

steps.name: Cheerful Infected
steps.text: Come, beautiful Fräulein, let us skip!

steps.name: Hibiscus
steps.text: But I really don't have the time, and I'm not much of a danc—

steps.name: Cheerful Infected
steps.text: No worries, we all dance poorly at times. No one will laugh at you.

steps.name: Passionate Infected
steps.text: Very well, I'll play this in three...

steps.name: Passionate Infected
steps.text: One-two-three, one-two-three... ready—go!

steps.name: Hibiscus
steps.text: I'm sorry, I trod on you so many...

steps.name: Cheerful Infected
steps.text: That's fine, I'm delighted to dance with you! Thank you for joining us!

steps.name: Passionate Infected
steps.text: Goodbye! Have a beautiful day!

steps.name: Cheerful Infected
steps.text: Welcome to the Afterglow!

steps.name: Hibiscus
steps.text: Thank you, thanks.

steps.name: Woman in Operator Attire
steps.text: Good morning, Hibiscus~

steps.name: Hibiscus
steps.text: You're... Andante? From the branch?

steps.name: Andante
steps.text: That's right! Welcome to Vyseheim's Afterglow!

steps.name: Hibiscus
steps.text: Thank you. This is awkward, you coming out here just to greet me.

steps.name: Andante
steps.text: I didn't come just to greet you.

steps.name: Hibiscus
steps.text: Eh?

steps.name: Andante
steps.text: Word came that before you left for the Afterglow, you were piling pressure on yourself, staying up all hours of every night. You were reading papers right up until you left the landship.

steps.name: Andante
steps.text: So today, your job is entirely to relax!

steps.name: Hibiscus
steps.text: I'm actually fine.

steps.name: Andante
steps.text: No, can't have that! Strings snap when you stretch them that thin!

steps.name: Andante
steps.text: Besides, you came just at the right time. Herr Czerny's farewell concert is in a week, and it just so happens today's application day.

steps.name: Andante
steps.text: Apparently, he's performing at the plaza in front of Afterglow Hall! It'll be over if we're a moment too late!

steps.name: Hibiscus
steps.text: But the mission...

steps.name: Andante
steps.text: If this chance goes, it's gone! We can talk missions tomorrow! Let's run!

steps.name: Andante
steps.text: We're here!

steps.name: Andante
steps.text: Afterglow Hall. They say it's this very concert hall the Afterglow gets its name from.

steps.name: Hibiscus
steps.text: Is... this even a building, or is it a giant instrument...?

steps.name: Andante
steps.text: Enough, the Hall's not going anywhere, we'll have time to admire it later. Our focus today is Herr Czerny.

steps.name: Hibiscus
steps.text: I think... I read about Mister, Herr Czerny beforehand. He was born in the Afterglow?

steps.name: Andante
steps.text: He was. He's still the one and only musician ever to both be Infected and renowned in Leithanien. He's even held minor tours around the country—

steps.name: Andante
steps.text: I see him, there he is!
The musician stands on the steps outside the hall, a colossal instrument his height upright beside him.
No one stands in the five-meter semicircle around him.
Outside that semicircle, the crowds teem.

steps.name: Andante
steps.text: Blow me down! Half of the Afterglow's here, at least.

steps.name: Hibiscus
steps.text: Half?!

steps.name: Andante
steps.text: Herr Czerny used to constantly perform outdoors here, but he's been ill for half a year, and it's his first time back. You don't know how excited everyone is—

steps.name: Andante
steps.text: (Whisper) It's starting.
With the sound of a piano, the plaza quickly falls to a hush.
Practically everyone stops talking.
Even the peddler hawking incessantly until now lowers his voice.
The song is short.
The moment Czerny's performance ends, a mountainous applause erupts.
It gradually abates. While Czerny prepares to play the next song, someone neatly dressed squeezes through the crowd, and arrives at his side.

steps.name: Frivolous Noble
steps.text: Herr Czerny, Dame Gertrude sends her regards.

steps.name: Czerny
steps.text: Oh. You, I see.

steps.name: Frivolous Noble
steps.text: She asks me to remind you that be it an applicational affair or the concert day itself, you haven't been booked for an outdoor performance.

steps.name: Czerny
steps.text: And what does it matter?

steps.name: Czerny
steps.text: Other places may have their schedules, but you are hard-pressed to stop me performing for all in the Afterglow.

steps.name: Frivolous Noble
steps.text: Your health isn't the fairest. You'd best not tire yourself too much...

steps.name: Czerny
steps.text: I know my health best. If I didn't feel better today, I wouldn't be here.

steps.name: Czerny
steps.text: Go tell Gertrude: mind her own business. Don't come all persnickety at me.

steps.name: Frivolous Noble
steps.text: Very well.

steps.name: Hibiscus
steps.text: What was his problem? Why did no one say anything?

steps.name: Andante
steps.text: He's a retainer of Dame Gertrude Strollo.

steps.name: Hibiscus
steps.text: Gertrude Strollo... Countess Strollo, the ruler... the Lehnsfrau of Vyseheim?

steps.name: Andante
steps.text: The very same.

steps.name: Andante
steps.text: But Herr Czerny sent that man packing in just a few words! What a feel-good sight.

steps.name: Hibiscus
steps.text: I see.

steps.name: Andante
steps.text: Let's head into Afterglow Hall in a moment. Application's about to begin.
Seeing the noble's figure disappear into the crowd, Czerny clears his throat.

steps.name: Czerny
steps.text: Thank you all for your support.

steps.name: Czerny
steps.text: Today, I came not just to play you all a passage or two, long while that it's been, but to warm up for the concert next week.

steps.name: Czerny
steps.text: I invite you all to be enthusiastic in this application. Prove your love for music on the stage. I'll be here, supporting you all.

steps.name: Czerny
steps.text: I'll be at the selections tomorrow too, casting my own discerning eye.

steps.name: Czerny
steps.text: Now, let me play a few more pieces for you all. I welcome you to bring out whatever instruments you're good with. Whether you accompany me or play by your own tune, I welcome it all.

steps.name: Czerny
steps.text: Thank you, everyone!
Czerny bows, the heavy silence finally lifts, and the crowd erupts into even more fervorous applause.

steps.name: Food Stall Owner
steps.text: Hey. You set up shop here too?

steps.name: Coffee Shop Owner
steps.text: Damn near everyone's here at the Hall. Where else am I going to do business if not here?

steps.name: Food Stall Owner
steps.text: Sure, but I don't think anyone's willing to drink your coffee.

steps.name: Coffee Shop Owner
steps.text: Easy for you to say—

steps.name: Infected
steps.text: Excuse me, I'll take a tub of sauerkraut. A big one!

steps.name: Food Stall Owner
steps.text: Coming up!

steps.name: Coffee Shop Owner
steps.text: A crowd full of anticipation, a musician forcing his ailing body along, a noble given the cold shoulder...

steps.name: Coffee Shop Owner
steps.text: (Whisper) Touches my heart.

steps.name: Disgruntled Old Man
steps.text: Kreide. You still insist on applying to that concert?

steps.name: Kreide
steps.text: Yes, I do want to go...

steps.name: Disgruntled Old Man
steps.text: Fine. Don't often see you turning a deaf ear like this. You want to go, go.

steps.name: Kreide
steps.text: Thank you, Grandpa!

steps.name: Grandpa
steps.text: You sign up and come straight back, don't linger outside.

steps.name: Kreide
steps.text: I'll try.

steps.name: Grandpa
steps.text: Try?

steps.name: Kreide
steps.text: Apparently, entrants have to perform onstage for this application, so they can prove their skill...

steps.name: Grandpa
steps.text: But your cello's been wrecked forever. You only have the one string to play. What are you doing about that?

steps.name: Kreide
steps.text: It's alright, they'll provide a loaner instrument.

steps.name: Grandpa
steps.text: *sigh* Very, very thoughtful of them. Why did nobody tell me, hm?

steps.name: Kreide
steps.text: Grandpa, are you... mad?

steps.name: Grandpa
steps.text: What? No, I'm just a little uneasy about it.

steps.name: Kreide
steps.text: I promise, I'll be back as soon as the application's over. I won't run off anywhere!

steps.name: Grandpa
steps.text: Fine, fine, I hear you.

steps.name: Kreide
steps.text: I'll put the tea by the stove, now. Remember to drink it soon, don't let it get cold!

steps.name: Mature Noble
steps.text: Application's beginning soon. It's about time you went.

steps.name: Young Noble
steps.text: I still can't swallow this. You called me here, all the way from Urtica, specifically to have me apply to this concert full of Infected?

steps.name: Mature Noble
steps.text: Such a level of interaction with Infected won't pose any risk.

steps.name: Young Noble
steps.text: You don't have to tell me. I know.

steps.name: Young Noble
steps.text: What I mean to say is, I don't understand why you invited me here just for some run-of-the-mill concert.

steps.name: Mature Noble
steps.text: You've always wanted to breathe the air of freedom, haven't you?

steps.name: Young Noble
steps.text: I can't deny that, but—

steps.name: Mature Noble
steps.text: Don't let doubts overtake you now. Enjoy the commoners' festive atmosphere.

steps.name: Young Noble
steps.text: (Shrug)

steps.name: Mature Noble
steps.text: The car is ready for you. There's some way to travel from the Cliffy Patio to the Afterglow; I recommend you not go on foot, so as not to affect your performance at application.

steps.name: Young Noble
steps.text: I appreciate your kindness. Farewell, Strollo—

steps.name: Mature Noble
steps.text: You're forgetting. I prefer my given name, not my surname.

steps.name: Young Noble
steps.text: I apologize, Dame Gertrude.

steps.name: Hibiscus
steps.text: What a queue!

steps.name: Andante
steps.text: That's the line for application. We're just going with the crowds, so come this way~

steps.name: Kreide
steps.text: Hello, can I ask...?

steps.name: Worn-out Infected
steps.text: Here to apply, right? End of the line's there. Head over and queue up.

steps.name: Kreide
steps.text: —It's so long!

steps.name: Worn-out Infected
steps.text: Plenty of folk started queueing before the sun came up.

steps.name: Kreide
steps.text: But I'm really in a rush to get my application over with. I'm still caring for my grandpa back home.

steps.name: Worn-out Infected
steps.text: No can do. Look, we're all Afterglowers. Who hasn't got someone to care for at home?

steps.name: Kreide
steps.text: Well... but...

steps.name: Worn-out Infected
steps.text: Get in line, quick. It'll be even longer soon enough.

steps.name: Young Noble
steps.text: Can you really not accommodate, just this once?

steps.name: Worn-out Infected
steps.text: I said no. That's just—

steps.name: Worn-out Infected
steps.text: Wait, y—you're a noble, aren't you? You're here to apply to our concert?!

steps.name: Young Noble
steps.text: If you see as much, then could you oblige myself and my friend here?

steps.name: Worn-out Infected
steps.text: But we've got rules...

steps.name: Young Noble
steps.text: Or do you plan to refuse a noble's sincerest request?

steps.name: Worn-out Infected
steps.text: I wouldn't dare.

steps.name: Young Noble
steps.text: Thank you for your understanding.

steps.name: Young Noble
steps.text: Come, now.

steps.name: Young Noble
steps.text: Didn't you hear me? They're letting us through.

steps.name: Kreide
steps.text: A... Alright!

steps.name: Kreide
steps.text: But—

steps.name: Kreide
steps.text: Er, where'd he go?

steps.name: Mannered Infected
steps.text: Next, please.

steps.name: Mannered Infected
steps.text: Can I have your name, please?

steps.name: Kreide
steps.text: People call me Kreide.

steps.name: Mannered Infected
steps.text: What instruments are you proficient in?

steps.name: Kreide
steps.text: The cello.

steps.name: Mannered Infected
steps.text: Did you come without your own cello?

steps.name: Kreide
steps.text: I don't have one...

steps.name: Mannered Infected
steps.text: That's fine, we provide common-use instruments to musicians. You can access them at your leisure.

steps.name: Mannered Infected
steps.text: Alright, you may begin. Be careful not to go over one minute.

steps.name: Mannered Infected
steps.text: Is there a problem?

steps.name: Kreide
steps.text: I didn't get to ask just now, but how do you determine pay for participation?

steps.name: Mannered Infected
steps.text: Pay?

steps.name: Kreide
steps.text: Eh?

steps.name: Kreide
steps.text: The person who told me about the concert said that so long as I was chosen, I'd get ample pay.

steps.name: Kreide
steps.text: My grandpa's gravely ill, and I need money for his treatment.

steps.name: Mannered Infected
steps.text: I sympathize with your plight, but there is no material reward for this concert.

steps.name: Kreide
steps.text: There's no pay at all?!

steps.name: Mannered Infected
steps.text: I believe the vast majority feel that the ultimate honorarium comes from performing with Herr Czerny at his farewell concert.

steps.name: Kreide
steps.text: How could this be...?

steps.name: Mannered Infected
steps.text: It's your decision to perform or not. However, if you do decide to leave, I hope for you to at least leave us with a fine melody before you do.

steps.name: Kreide
steps.text: I... alright.
Kreide, somewhat dejectedly, bows.
He slowly takes a seat, and steadies the cello between his knees.
With a hand on his bow, and the other on the strings, the dismay is all but swept from his face, leaving only concentration.
From the cello's strings flows an ornate melody, gradually filling the whole hall.
After a number of bars, Kreide's performance reaches its sweetest point, when a concert flute joins from below the stage out of nowhere.
The noble in black plays the flute, accompanying Kreide's cello, and he paces his way onto the stage.
Kreide is briefly startled, but nevertheless concludes the passage with his own cadence, while the noble follows the cello's ending with his own, briefest cadenza.

steps.name: Mannered Infected
steps.text: And that's one minute.

steps.name: Mannered Infected
steps.text: That was the most beautiful performance I've heard today.

steps.name: Mannered Infected
steps.text: I feel we should pay our respects to both you young men.

steps.name: Mannered Infected
steps.text: Are you here to apply to this concert too?

steps.name: Young Noble
steps.text: The very same.

steps.name: Young Noble
steps.text: I was planning to do so alone, but professedly, Herr Kreide's performance struck me deep, and I did happen to meet him earlier.

steps.name: Young Noble
steps.text: I was loath to miss a chance to perform with such a superb instrumentalist.

steps.name: Mannered Infected
steps.text: Understood. May I have your name?

steps.name: Young Noble
steps.text: Ebenholz.

steps.name: Mannered Infected
steps.text: To have someone like y... Ebenholz?

steps.name: Mannered Infected
steps.text: Are you certain? Your real name is Ebenholz? That's not an alias you just came up with after staring at the piano?

steps.name: Ebenholz
steps.text: You really are too mistrustful.

steps.name: Ebenholz
steps.text: Besides, a piano isn't the only thing with keys. Does a flute not have them too?

steps.name: Mannered Infected
steps.text: Even so, your lineage and estate—

steps.name: Ebenholz
steps.text: I'll say again, my name is Ebenholz. Do you have any other questions?

steps.name: Mannered Infected
steps.text: Very well.

steps.name: Mannered Infected
steps.text: That said, since you and Herr Kreide brought no agreement on whether to apply as an ensemble, the decision lies with him.

steps.name: Mannered Infected
steps.text: Herr Kreide, what do you feel?

steps.name: Kreide
steps.text: I was only applying to this concert... for my grandpa's medical fees...

steps.name: Ebenholz
steps.text: Should Kreide assent to an ensemble, I'd be very willing to provide him and his grandfather economic assistance.

steps.name: Kreide
steps.text: —Really?

steps.name: Mannered Infected
steps.text: That kind of aid doesn't come without strings attached. Make sure you're completely clear about this.

steps.name: Mannered Infected
steps.text: We saw a musician swindled last year. He signed an extremely unfair contract...

steps.name: Ebenholz
steps.text: Please, I ask for some respect.

steps.name: Kreide
steps.text: I'll do it!

steps.name: Mannered Infected
steps.text: Then I'll leave it at that.

steps.name: Mannered Infected
steps.text: If the two of you are entering the selections as flute and cello, then the one choice you have is 'Morgen und Abend.'

steps.name: Mannered Infected
steps.text: It's a duet for flute and cello with piano accompaniment, and one of Herr Czerny's signature works. Are you okay with that?

steps.name: Ebenholz
steps.text: Said piece marked a turning point in my learning flute. I'm extraordinarily honored that I may perform it on Herr Czerny's stage.

steps.name: Kreide
steps.text: I'm fine with it, too!

steps.name: Hibiscus
steps.text: Why is that noble helping Kreide?

steps.name: Andante
steps.text: A lot of musicians have nobles as backers. Nothing strange about it.

steps.name: Andante
steps.text: Some do it because they're not good enough themselves, so they see a really skilled musician and leap for them. They like how it makes them look better all around.

steps.name: Andante
steps.text: I can't figure out this Ebenholz either, though. Maybe he is just appreciating a fellow maestro.

steps.name: Hibiscus
steps.text: Something still doesn't sit too well with me.

steps.name: Hibiscus
steps.text: Oh, we could treat Kreide's grandpa—

steps.name: Andante
steps.text: Hibiscus, you were here to investigate the Serendipitous Infected Prognosis Phenomenon, weren't you?

steps.name: Hibiscus
steps.text: Erk.

steps.name: Andante
steps.text: And our branch is too small. We don't have what it takes to admit patients like a hospital.

steps.name: Andante
steps.text: Examinations, diagnoses, prescriptions for milder cases, getting patients in touch with other organizations when they need hospitalization—that's our limit.

steps.name: Hibiscus
steps.text: But I'm still a little worried.

steps.name: Andante
steps.text: In that case... Kreide's application is over, anyhow. Let's go catch up and ask him, see if we can offer him any help, okay?

steps.name: Andante
steps.text: Test results are in. Cell-Originium Assimilation is 8%, Blood Originium-Crystal Density is 0.23u/L... I can't say it's too severe, but it's not good by any stretch.

steps.name: Andante
steps.text: Typically, any patient should receive standard treatment with indicators at this level, no matter how they feel themselves. I suggest hospitalized recovery.

steps.name: Grandpa
steps.text: Standard treatment, hospitalized recovery...

steps.name: Grandpa
steps.text: I hear Rhodes Island is just as much a business. You might be pitying me, giving me the test with no charge, but there's no such thing as a free lunch for me, eh?

steps.name: Andante
steps.text: We're partnered with some organizations in Vyseheim. We can refer patients to them.

steps.name: Andante
steps.text: They have collaborative protocols in place with Rhodes Island. The prices will be cheaper compared to anywhere else.

steps.name: Andante
steps.text: Given your present circumstances, I can try to talk down their fees further, or I could help offset expenses on both sides...

steps.name: Grandpa
steps.text: No need.

steps.name: Grandpa
steps.text: If I knew Kreide was only going for my sake, I wouldn't have let him go, no matter what.

steps.name: Grandpa
steps.text: Kreide. I'll say it again. You return every last cent to that noble. We're going.

steps.name: Grandpa
steps.text: What could possibly be happening behind you when an aristocrat gives you money for no good reason?

steps.name: Kreide
steps.text: But Ebenholz just wants me to perform with him.

steps.name: Grandpa
steps.text: Even if he means no harm, he—

steps.name: Grandpa
steps.text: *sigh* He might mean no harm, and an old man like me totting about without any grand standing or friend in power won't be worth much to exploit.

steps.name: Grandpa
steps.text: The hospitals still wouldn't be angels to me, even if they do admit me. I don't want my life depending on their whimsy.

steps.name: Grandpa
steps.text: If you see a heart of gold in that little lord, then use that money for your own sake. Do some business that lets you get on with your life.

steps.name: Kreide
steps.text: No. I already agreed with Ebenholz. The money he gives me is for treating your sickness!

steps.name: Grandpa
steps.text: You're tired of me. Throwing me into hospital so you can never look back, isn't that right?

steps.name: Kreide
steps.text: What? How could I...

steps.name: Hibiscus
steps.text: How about he convalesces here, instead of going to any partners?

steps.name: Andante
steps.text: Hibiscus, I understand how you feel... but we don't have beds here, and our medication stores are for emergency response.

steps.name: Hibiscus
steps.text: If we can have him recovering here, we'll be able to monitor his health condition more tightly. I'm sure it'd be of help to our investigation too.

steps.name: Hibiscus
steps.text: I can clear my own guest bed for him to take. Medication-wise, we'll sell at our partners' prices. I'll write a report after the fact explaining the situation.

steps.name: Hibiscus
steps.text: That should all be watertight under procedure, right?

steps.name: Andante
steps.text: I think... that works out.

steps.name: Hibiscus
steps.text: Then we're all good to go on our end. Sir, how about you? Are you able to accept that?

steps.name: Hibiscus
steps.text: I guarantee, your treatment will be highest priority for us. All research propositions will hinge on informed consent, and we'll never commit to anything harmful to your health.

steps.name: Kreide
steps.text: I agree!

steps.name: Kreide
steps.text: And I have to rehearse with Ebenholz soon, too. I might not have too much time to look after you.

steps.name: Kreide
steps.text: Besides, conditions here are so much better than at home. If you're here, I can put my heart at ease too... please, Grandpa!

steps.name: Grandpa
steps.text: *sigh*.

steps.name: Grandpa
steps.text: I'll go home this evening to pack some things. I'll be back tomorrow morning. You'll let me have that much, won't you?
